 Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati
Judgment Reserved on 01/06/2023 Pronounced on 06/06/2023
1.

This writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred claiming the following reliefs:
"It is therefore most humbly prayed that this writ petition may kindly be allowed:-
a.

That by an appropriate writ, order or direction may kindly be issued and the act of respondents with regard to construct the CHC Building upon the land of khasra no.58 Rakba 0.4654 Hectare (3.10 Bigha) village Dungra Chhota, Tehsil Sajjangarh,
District Banswara may kindly be declared illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional. b.
That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and the respondents may kindly be prohibited to construct the CHC Building upon the land of khasra no.58 Rakba 0.4654 Hectare (3.10 Bigha) village (D.B. SAW/542/2023 has been filed in this matter.
Please refer the same for further orders)

sentences.text: [CW-7228/2023] Dungra Chhota, Tehsil Sajjangarh, District Banswara and further direct to restore the position of the land while remove the material laying upon the land of the petitioner.

c. That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and the respondents may kindly be restrained for any kind of interference in the use and occupation right of the petitioner with regard to land in question without proper acquisition if same is required under a larger public interest.

d. Any other relief, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit to protect and maintained the healthy judicial system in State of Rajasthan, by which the petitioner may get full justice, may also be allowed."

2. Brief facts of the case, as placed before this Court by learned counsel for the petitioner, are that the petitioner was having an agricultural land comprising khasra no.58 rakba 3.10 bigha (land in question), kism as Bhuri-I Magri at Village Dungra Chhota, Patwar Circle, Dungra Chhota, Tehsil Sajjangarh, District Banswara.

2.1 The District Collector, Banswara, vide order dated 28.06.2022, allotted a land comprising khasra no.78/26 (old khasra no.26) rakba 0.8094 hectare, for the purpose of construction of the Community Heath Centre (CHC) Building at Dungra Chhota; prior to such allotment, the said land was entered in the name of the Police Station at Sajjangarh. 2.2.

Thereafter, the respondent-Department approved the site and handed over the same for construction of the CHC Building to the executing agency; the construction of the CHC Building was started over the land in question, whereas the land allotted for the said purpose was comprising khasra No.78/26.
Thereupon, the (D.B. SAW/542/2023 has been filed in this matter.

Please refer the same for further orders) (3 of 5) [CW-7228/2023] petitioner served a legal notice through his Advocate to the respondents for stopping the construction work over the land in question.

Despite service of such notice, when the construction work was not stopped, the matter was brought to the notice of the District Collector on 12.04.2023 and submitted a detailed representation against the construction of the CHC Building over the land in question.

2.3. The District Collector, Banswara passed an order for conducting an inquiry into the matter,
whereupon, the Tehsildar concerned directed the local inspector to conduct the survey; the survey report dated 13.04.2023 so submitted, recorded the construction of the CHC Building over the land in question, i.e. the land comprising Khasra no. 58, belonging to the petitioner.

2.4. Since thereafter also, the grievance of the petitioner was not redressed by the respondents, the present petition,
laying challenge to the impugned action on the part of the respondents, has been preferred, claiming the afore-quoted reliefs.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that a specific and lawful objection against the construction in question was taken by the petitioner before the respondents, but despite the same,
the respondents are going to complete the construction work of the CHC Building over the land in question, which is not justified in law.

3.1. Learned counsel further submitted that apparently, the land allotted for construction of the CHC Building is situated far away from the land in question of the petitioner, but the respondents (D.B.
SAW/542/2023 has been filed in this matter.
Please refer the same for further orders) (4 of 5)
[CW-7228/2023] approved site for such construction, which is different from the land allotted for the said purpose.

3.2. Learned counsel also submitted that as per Section 2 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, if, amongst others,
for any public purpose, the appropriate Government, wishes to acquire a land, then prior thereto, it is mandatory to conduct proceedings under the said Act.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Furthermore, as per learned counsel, there was no proposal of the revenue department for setting apart or acquiring the land in question, for any purpose.
4.

On the Other hand, learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents,
while opposing the aforesaid submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the land in question has been allotted by the concerned authority, for the specific purpose of construction of the CHC Building, for providing better facilities to the public at large.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties as well as perused the record of the case.
6.

This Court observes that the land in question has been allotted by the District Collector, Banswara for the purpose of construction of CHC Building; and earlier the same land had been allotted for construction of the Police Station at Sajjangarh, however, such allotment of the land for the police station has been cancelled by the District Collector himself, while allotting the said land to the Medical and Heath Department for the construction in question.
(D.B. SAW/542/2023 has been filed in this matter.
Please refer the same for further orders) (5 of 5)

This Court further observes that the land in question has been allotted to the Medical and Heath Department for construction of CHC Building under the Rajasthan Land Revenue (Allotment of Unoccupied Government Agricultural Lands for the Construction of Schools, Colleges, Dispensaries,
Dharamshalas & Other Buildings of Public Utility) Rules, 1963, which is perfectly justified, more particularly, in view of the fact that the same was done for the benefit of the public at large.
8.

entities.text:
Rajasthan Land Revenue (Allotment of Unoccupied Government Agricultural Lands for the Construction of Schools, Colleges, Dispensaries,
Dharamshalas & Other Buildings of Public Utility) Rules, 1963
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In light of the aforesaid observations and looking into the factual matrix of the present case, this Court does not find it a fit case so as to grant any relief to the petitioner in the present petition.
9. Consequently, the present petition is dismissed.
All pending applications stand disposed of.

(DR.PUSHPENDRA SINGH BHATI), J.
